items.title: 73243_Joe Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Our families, they all knew each other. This lady was 91 years old. Her name was Mrs. Gleason Neesen

ctx.x: You finish it up the player piano.

Yes. Well, the player piano -- this lady here, B. Walker comes by the house. There's a lady out here wants to see Joe. So I said, 'Well, fine.' Some pretty little chick stop by to see me, you know, even my wife can't resist that. You know I'm home but second time in 22 years. And had a most delicate and complete surprise I ever had in my life. This lady in our home we played -- she had two daughters -- Piano Rose (or piano rolls). Our families, they all knew each other. This lady was 91 years old. Her name was…

Now, see we had in Webster Groves, or outside Webster Groves they had things called roadhouses. I don't know if you know what a roadhouse is. Well, you might have an idea about it. A roadhouse in those days, Stan, at least the ones I played, there were fellows that had their families there, they might have had some other businesses but that was their love. That was their love, that was their instrument, you know. So, still haven't got to Jeff City, have we?
